editorial.titleTr: Ruling Party Chief's Abuse of Power Scandal Erodes National Momentum
summaryTr: The ruling party leader faces declining support and weakened leadership amid controversy over abuse of power.
When a festival performance was interrupted by someone rushing onto the stage, the controversy grew until an apology was issued.
Visits to fire stations at dawn and parking in emergency zones demonstrate that responsible behavior is required.
editorial.bodyTr: The ruling party leader has become embroiled in multiple controversies, with concerns mounting over declining party approval ratings and weakened leadership. An incident at a regional festival where the leader took the stage without notice and disrupted an ongoing performance sparked growing allegations of abuse of power, eventually prompting an apology. These were followed by controversies over an unannounced visit to a fire station at dawn and improper parking in an emergency zone, raising calls for more responsible conduct befitting the ruling party's leader.

editorials.titleTr: Chinese Equipment Fills Army Operations Center: Security Concerns Raised
summaryTr: 16% of Army Operations Center videoconferencing equipment is Chinese-made
Information leakage risks remain despite relying solely on security inspections
Over 1,770 military CCTVs are also Chinese-made, stricter standards needed
editorials.bodyTr: Approximately 16 percent of the Army's video conferencing equipment is made in China and has been deployed in operational command centers. The Army claimed there are no problems through security inspections and control measures, but the video conferencing equipment still poses an information leakage risk. More than 1,770 Chinese-made CCTV cameras remain in military facilities, underscoring the need to raise security standards for critical installations.

editorials.titleTr: Anthropic's AI Mass Learning of Korean Books Raises Urgent Copyright Protection Concerns
summaryTr: Anthropic used 300,000 Korean books without authorization for AI training.
The publishing industry strongly demanded an end to illegal use and protection of copyrights.
Legal regulation of AI companies' unauthorized use of copyrighted works is urgently needed.
editorials.bodyTr: Evidence has emerged that U.S. AI company Anthropic unlawfully downloaded books by Korean authors to train its Claude model. According to reports, Anthropic secured approximately 300,000 Korean-language printed books after signing a contract with a domestic book distributor in 2024. The publishing industry has demanded disclosure of the works used and protection of intellectual property rights, calling for measures to prevent illegal use and ensure fair compensation.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] "North Korean Nukes Are Defensive Weapons"—A Dangerous Security Doctrine That Gambles on Intentions Over Adversary Capabilities
summaryTr: Lee Jae-myung defines North Korean nuclear weapons as 'defensive arms,' sparking security doctrine controversy
Must prepare for worst-case scenarios based on actual capabilities, not speculation about intentions
Critics slam security outlook that relies on luck while ignoring offensive military strategy
editorial.bodyTr: Despite North Korea's advancement of nuclear capabilities and its aggressive military strategy, President Lee Jae-myeong's national security perspective that defines North Korean nuclear weapons as defensive is problematic. National security must prepare for the worst-case scenario based on an adversary's actual capabilities rather than its stated intentions. This editorial emphasizes the importance of maintaining robust security posture through historical examples.

summaryTr: Financial Watchdog Chief Admits to Rushed Single-Stock Leveraged ETF Approval, Cutting Review Time by More Than Half
Reckless Speed-to-Market Strategy Triggers Trillions of Won in Losses for Retail Investors, Sparks Sharp KOSPI Decline
Calls for Thorough Investigation to Identify Those Responsible Amid Suspicions of Political Intent
editorials.bodyTr: FSS Governor Lee Bok-hyun admitted during a parliamentary audit that the review period for single-stock leveraged ETFs was cut to less than half the normal duration, resulting in rushed approval. Due to the aggressive timeline in the listing process, individual investors suffered losses in the trillions of won, and the product has been identified as a contributing factor to the sharp decline in the KOSPI. As suspicions mount regarding the forced listing based on political intentions, a thorough investigation into the facts is necessary to identify those responsible.

editorial.title: [사설] 프랑스 청년의 절망…한국은 다르다고 할 때 아니다
editorial.body: 입력 종합 26면 프랑스 청년들의 절망과 분노가 거리로 쏟아졌다. 지난 17일(현지시간) 전국 110곳에서 55만 명이 시위에 참여했고, 일부 지역에서는 방화와 약탈까지 벌어졌다. 알고 보면 예고된 위기의 현실화다. 프랑스는 재정적자가 눈덩이처럼 불어나 국가채무가 국내총생산(GDP)의 119%에 육박한다. 교육부 예산의 3분의 1가량이 퇴직 공무원 연금 지급에 쓰이지만, 정치권의 이해관계에 가로막혀 개혁은 중단됐다. 재정 압박 속에 교사 부족 등 교육 환경이 악화하자 청년들이 거리로 나섰다. 증세로 해결할 수도 없다. GDP 대비 조세부담률이 44%에 달하기 때문이다. 프랑스병(病)은 이렇게 원인을 알고도 못 고치는 난치병에 이르렀다. 위기의 근본 원인은 성장엔진 약화다. 프랑스의 올해 성장률 전망치는 0%대다. 구조개혁은 미루고 재정 지출만 늘리다 중국 수요에 기대던 명품 매출마저 줄어들자 막다른 골목에 몰렸다. 프랑스병은 2010년 남유럽 재정위기와도 닮았다. 산업 경쟁력은 취약한데 복지만 퍼붓다가 위기를 불렀다. 유럽 경제의 엔진인 독일마저 중국 전기차 공세에 밀려 자동차 공장을 줄줄이 폐쇄하고 있다. 서유럽 전체가 중국 시장에 기댄 수출, 러시아의 값싼 에너지, 미국에 의존한 안보라는 3대 버팀목에 매달리다가 흔들리고 있다. 한국은 다르다고 할 수 있을까. 국제통화기금(IMF)은 올해 한국 성장률 전망치를 3.3%로 높였다. 수출도 역대 최대 기록을 갈아치우고 1인당 국민소득은 4만 달러를 바라본다. 그러나 반도체 외줄타기 성장이다. 화려한 경제 지표와 달리 우리 청년들은 사회에 첫발조차 내딛기 어렵다. 지난달까지 청년 취업자 수는 47개월 연속 감소했다. 집값 급등으로 내 집 마련은 언감생심이고 전월세 부담도 버겁다. 프랑스병은 한국의 반면교사다. 정부는 반도체 세수만 믿고 미래대응기금까지 동원해 확장 재정에 나서고 있지만 인공지능(AI) 거품 붕괴 경고가 잇따른다. 반도체 호황이 꺾이면 성장과 세수가 동시에 흔들리게 된다. 정부는 재정을 쓰되 산업 경쟁력 강화와 청년 일자리 창출에 집중해야 한다. 프랑스 청년의 절망을 한국 청년들이 겪게 해선 안 된다.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: France's Youth in Despair... Now Is the Time to Acknowledge Korea's Differences
summaryTr: French youth's despair has erupted into street protests. Weak growth and delayed structural reforms are to blame.
As financial deterioration creates a vicious cycle of poor education and job scarcity, young people have lost hope.
South Korea risks falling into the same crisis if it relies solely on semiconductor booms.
editorial.bodyTr: French youth's despair and anger have spilled onto the streets. On the 17th, 550,000 people participated in protests at 110 locations nationwide, with arson and looting occurring in some areas. In retrospect, this is the realization of a crisis that was foreseeable. France's fiscal deficit has snowballed, with national debt approaching 119 percent of gross domestic product. About a third of the education ministry's budget is spent on pensions for retired civil servants, but reform has stalled due to political interests. As the educational environment deteriorated amid fiscal pressure, with teacher shortages and other issues, youth took to the streets. Tax increases cannot solve this either, as the tax-to-GDP ratio reaches 44 percent. France's malaise has become an intractable disease that cannot be cured despite knowing its causes. The fundamental cause of the crisis is weakening growth engines. France's growth forecast for this year stands in the zero percent range. With structural reforms postponed and only fiscal spending increased, the country has found itself in a dead end as luxury goods sales that relied on Chinese demand have also declined. French malaise resembles the 2008 sovereign debt crisis in Southern Europe. Weak industrial competitiveness combined with excessive welfare spending triggered crisis. Even Germany, the engine of European economy, is closing auto factories one after another, pushed back by China's electric vehicle offensive. All of Western Europe is faltering as it clings to three pillars: exports dependent on the Chinese market, cheap Russian energy, and security reliant on the United States. Can Korea claim to be different? The International Monetary Fund has raised Korea's growth forecast for this year to 3.3 percent. Exports are also breaking all-time records, and per capita income is approaching 40,000 dollars. Yet this is single-wire tightrope growth dependent on semiconductors. Contrary to stellar economic indicators, our youth struggle to even take their first steps into society. Through last month, youth employment numbers had declined for 47 consecutive months. With skyrocketing housing prices, owning a home is out of the question, and monthly rent burdens are heavy. French malaise is a cautionary tale for Korea. The government is relying solely on semiconductor tax revenues and even mobilizing future response funds to pursue expansionary fiscal policy, but warnings of an artificial intelligence bubble collapse keep mounting. Should the semiconductor boom falter, both growth and tax revenues will wobble simultaneously. The government must spend wisely but concentrate on strengthening industrial competitiveness and creating jobs for youth. Korean youth must not experience the despair that French youth are enduring.

leanScore.rationale: 구조개혁 미루고 복지만 퍼붓다가 위기를 불렀다는 프랑스 비판을 통해 재정지출 확대와 복지정책을 암묵적으로 비판하고, 산업경쟁력 강화 중심의 시장친화적 정책을 강조하는 보수적 프레이밍을 보임.

editorial.title: Hollow apology
editorial.body: Choo's grudging words raise questions about sincerity; Firefighters deserve adequate funding Gyeonggi Province Gov. Choo Mi-ae apologized four days after making a controversial remark that appeared to portray firefighters as a drain on public finances. Her belated apology, however, has only deepened doubts about her sincerity. Choo apologized on Saturday after paying her respects to Kim Jin-seok, a fire lieutenant who died from injuries sustained in a factory fire in Bucheon, Gyeonggi Province. “Since you want an apology, I sincerely apologize from the bottom of my heart,” she said. No one offering a heartfelt apology would begin with “Since you want an apology.” The phrase suggests she sees no reason to apologize, but is doing so merely to satisfy others. One cannot help wondering whether she would have let the matter pass had public outrage and firefighters’ demands for an apology not mounted. An apology made only under pressure can hardly be considered genuine. Choo made the original remark on Oct. 13 during a parliamentary audit of the Gyeonggi provincial government. When a lawmaker from the main opposition People Power Party called for the central government to shoulder a larger share of fire service funding, Choo said the fire service seemed to be “the biggest and most troublesome drain on public finances.” In context, she may not have intended to disparage firefighters personally. Nevertheless, comparing people who risk their lives battling fires to a financial drain was indefensible and disgraceful. Had Choo promptly acknowledged her mistake and apologized, the controversy might not have escalated. A firefighters’ union demanded an apology the following day, but she remained silent. That silence made her eventual apology seem all the more reluctant. The backlash intensified on Friday, when a factory fire in Bucheon injured five firefighters who had rushed in to rescue civilians. One of them, Lt. Kim, was taken to the hospital in cardiac arrest. Yet Choo showed no willingness to apologize when reporters asked at the scene whether she would retract her remark. “Let’s not talk about that,” she replied. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea, sensing mounting public anger, instead rushed to apologize on her behalf. In the early hours of Saturday, news broke that Kim had died from his injuries. As governor, Choo could hardly ignore the funeral of a firefighter who had died fighting a fire in her own province. Only when she visited the funeral did she offer her grudging apology: “Since you want an apology, I’ll apologize.” The delay was troubling enough, but the wording was even more disgraceful. Choo's original remark and subsequent apology raise serious questions about whether she possesses the qualities expected of a provincial governor. Given her distinguished career as a judge, six-term lawmaker, Cabinet minister and governor, one wonders whether years of success have made her so accustomed to authority that she no longer knows how to bow her head when she is wrong. If Choo wanted to correct the imbalance in fire service funding, she should have urged the central government to assume a greater share of the costs rather than denigrating firefighters. Although firefighters came under central government jurisdiction in 2020, central funding accounted for just 10.7 percent of the fire service budget last year. The fire service operates under a dysfunctional system in which local governments bear most of the funding burden despite having no authority over budget formulation or personnel management. Along with institutional reforms, the central government should assume a substantial share of the financial burden. Choo should be at the forefront of efforts to ensure that firefighters receive the support they need to perform their duties safely. Whenever a firefighter is killed or seriously injured in the line of duty, her description of the fire service as a “drain on public finances” will inevitably resurface. The backlash over an apology that rang hollow is also a consequence of her own words and conduct. editorials.title: Hollow apology
editorials.body: Choo's grudging words raise questions about sincerity; Firefighters deserve adequate funding Gyeonggi Province Gov. Choo Mi-ae apologized four days after making a controversial remark that appeared to portray firefighters as a drain on public finances. Her belated apology, however, has only deepened doubts about her sincerity. Choo apologized on Saturday after paying her respects to Kim Jin-seok, a fire lieutenant who died from injuries sustained in a factory fire in Bucheon, Gyeonggi Province. “Since you want an apology, I sincerely apologize from the bottom of my heart,” she said. No one offering a heartfelt apology would begin with “Since you want an apology.” The phrase suggests she sees no reason to apologize, but is doing so merely to satisfy others. One cannot help wondering whether she would have let the matter pass had public outrage and firefighters’ demands for an apology not mounted. An apology made only under pressure can hardly be considered genuine. Choo made the original remark on Oct. 13 during a parliamentary audit of the Gyeonggi provincial government. When a lawmaker from the main opposition People Power Party called for the central government to shoulder a larger share of fire service funding, Choo said the fire service seemed to be “the biggest and most troublesome drain on public finances.” In context, she may not have intended to disparage firefighters personally. Nevertheless, comparing people who risk their lives battling fires to a financial drain was indefensible and disgraceful. Had Choo promptly acknowledged her mistake and apologized, the controversy might not have escalated. A firefighters’ union demanded an apology the following day, but she remained silent. That silence made her eventual apology seem all the more reluctant. The backlash intensified on Friday, when a factory fire in Bucheon injured five firefighters who had rushed in to rescue civilians. One of them, Lt. Kim, was taken to the hospital in cardiac arrest. Yet Choo showed no willingness to apologize when reporters asked at the scene whether she would retract her remark. “Let’s not talk about that,” she replied. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea, sensing mounting public anger, instead rushed to apologize on her behalf. In the early hours of Saturday, news broke that Kim had died from his injuries. As governor, Choo could hardly ignore the funeral of a firefighter who had died fighting a fire in her own province. Only when she visited the funeral did she offer her grudging apology: “Since you want an apology, I’ll apologize.” The delay was troubling enough, but the wording was even more disgraceful. Choo's original remark and subsequent apology raise serious questions about whether she possesses the qualities expected of a provincial governor. Given her distinguished career as a judge, six-term lawmaker, Cabinet minister and governor, one wonders whether years of success have made her so accustomed to authority that she no longer knows how to bow her head when she is wrong. If Choo wanted to correct the imbalance in fire service funding, she should have urged the central government to assume a greater share of the costs rather than denigrating firefighters. Although firefighters came under central government jurisdiction in 2020, central funding accounted for just 10.7 percent of the fire service budget last year. The fire service operates under a dysfunctional system in which local governments bear most of the funding burden despite having no authority over budget formulation or personnel management. Along with institutional reforms, the central government should assume a substantial share of the financial burden. Choo should be at the forefront of efforts to ensure that firefighters receive the support they need to perform their duties safely. Whenever a firefighter is killed or seriously injured in the line of duty, her description of the fire service as a “drain on public finances” will inevitably resurface. The backlash over an apology that rang hollow is also a consequence of her own words and conduct.
